newsitem.title: USA: USDA won't alter crop insurance for Alabama cotton.
newsitem.headline: USDA won't alter crop insurance for Alabama cotton.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department on Tuesday refused a request from Northern Alabama cotton producers to use an alternative method for calculating crop losses under the federal crop insurance program.
Cool, wet conditions in Northern Alabama this year have stunted crop development.

Neverless, current indications are that 75 percent of the cotton acreage will be harvested, "so we will not change the standard method of cotton loss adjustment," USDA Risk Management Adminstrator Ken Ackerman said in a statement.

This early in the growing season, loss adjusters typically use an appraisal method to calculate losses. That approach assumes normal weather and predicts yields based on the number of live plants in the field.

USDA sometimes allows crop insurance adjustors to deviate from that method. But that's only when losses are widespread and there is little chance that production will result from continued crop management, USDA said.
"Our goal over the next two weeks will be to work with insurance providers to ensure that producers who want an appraisal can get one," Ackerman said.
The Risk Management Agency will continue to monitor Northern Alabama crop connditions and take further action if warranted, Ackerman said.
